claims.statement: Locke distinguishes identity of person, human animal and substance; personal identity follows consciousness extending to past acts rather than sameness of material particles or soul alone.
limitations: Attribution supported in Bennett modernization; correct criterion remains contested.

claims.statement: Locke explicitly considers forgetfulness, sleep, changing substances and a prince/cobbler transfer; the transfer is a conditional illustration, not an observed result.
limitations: Consciousness cannot simply be replaced with a present inventory of memories; §20 responds to irreversible forgetting by distinguishing person from man.

claims.statement: An animal can persist without the current psychological features by which it is recognized; Olson argues that a human person is numerically the thinking animal, while the exact persistence conditions of animals require further premises.
limitations: Attribution, not established universal biological or metaphysical theorem.

claims.statement: Olson makes the unique-thinker premise explicit and challenges denials of animal thought or proposals of coincident thinkers; the transplant objection remains a competing conditional judgment.
limitations: His reconstruction of other authors is not a direct inspection of their originals.

claims.statement: Swinburne uses a hypothetical split into equally psychologically supported successors to argue for an unobserved immaterial identity-bearing part.
limitations: Short author essay; surgical feasibility and exhaustive physical description are assumed for analysis, not verified.

claims.statement: The simple-subject inference requires more than inability to identify a successor: it needs determinate further identity facts, their compatibility with the stipulated total evidence, and a reason those facts require an immaterial bearer.
alternative_explanations: Epistemic ignorance need not entail an additional substance; a reductionist can reject the further-fact premise.
limitations: Project objection and strongest charitable reconstruction, not an inspected technical reply by Swinburne.

claims.statement: If two successors are distinct, strict numerical identity cannot identify both with the one predecessor; branch-preserving concern or psychological succession uses a different relation.
alternative_explanations: A nonbranching criterion, a unique bearer rule, or an explicitly revised successor relation.
limitations: Conditional analysis; no metaphysical actuality follows.

claims.statement: Defining genuine memory as memory of one’s own past can presuppose the identity it purports to establish; a causal quasi-memory criterion must specify a link independently of sameness of person.
alternative_explanations: Psychological continuity through overlapping causal links may avoid requiring every later stage to remember every earlier stage.
limitations: Project-authored logical analysis; no inspected attribution to Parfit, Butler or Reid.

claims.statement: Interrupted awareness or ordinary forgetting does not alone decide persistence: an organism, simple subject, or adequately continuous psychological history may bridge the gap under different assumptions.
alternative_explanations: An experience-bundle account may set different persistence conditions.
limitations: No inference that lack of report measures total absence of experience; no proof that bridging sleep also bridges death.

claims.statement: Greyson1990 broadens the time item: the highest response groups apparent simultaneity, stopped time and time losing meaning. It is not a count of one uniquely defined timeless experience.
source_locators: p153 response alternatives; p156 Table1; p160 discussion
limitations: Original1983validation not reinspected; categories here are the1990modification.

claims.statement: Timmermann2018 reports all13 DMT participants meeting the scale threshold, compared with one at threshold after placebo; these are repeated conditions in13people, not26independent people.
source_locators: Methods; Results DMT Induces Near-Death Type Experiences
limitations: Fixed placebo-first order, single blinding, prior psychedelic experience and heterogeneous doses limit interpretation.

claims.statement: The DMT study’s time-item means were1.15(SD0.80) under DMT and1.54(SD0.78) in its13-person NDE comparator; Table1 supplies scores, not response-category counts.
source_locators: Table1 time row; Methods comparison group
limitations: No reconstructed numerator for stopped time, simultaneity or loss of meaning. Non-significance is not an equivalence test.

claims.statement: Phenomenological overlap after DMT shows that similar scale endorsements can arise in a drug context; it does not establish endogenous DMT as any particular NDE’s cause or explain away every anomalous detail.
alternative_explanations: A survival model could treat drugs as changing access to experience; this requires additional discriminating predictions.
limitations: No identified common mechanism, irreversibly dead subject, or ontological timelessness.

claims.statement: Alexander’s reviewed altered-duration account concerns remembered phenomenology; months/years seeming to pass is not the same claim as no intrinsic succession.
limitations: Inherited reviewed attribution, not new transcript inspection or independent event; recording alignment remains unverified.

claims.statement: Resuscitated-subject reports and aggregate brain-monitoring records do not by themselves supply H-S’s irreversible-death boundary, episode-specific experience timing or numerical-identity bridge.
source_locators: Inherited T07report and CL-T07-015; no new original inspection
alternative_explanations: Better timed verified information and explicit identity evidence could strengthen a narrower brain-independence inference.
limitations: Neither missing monitoring nor aggregate EEG establishes absence of all relevant processing.

claims.statement: M1 permits temporal personal continuation without timeless persons; M2 adds a timeless foundation grounding temporal persons, but individual survival remains an additional condition.
limitations: Project T01 model evaluation; foundation need not acquire states when temporal persons learn.

claims.statement: An enlarged M3 history can satisfy H-S if it contains actual subjectivity beyond the bodily-life boundary unified with the embodied life by a defensible identity relation, even if the foundation has no intrinsic succession.
alternative_explanations: A complete representation may be another subject’s knowledge rather than the individual’s continued experience.
limitations: Conditional coherent proposal, not proof of actual extension; beyond must be specified relationally if not temporally.

claims.statement: M4 can preserve information, represented relationships or value while the original subject ceases; a conscious foundation’s awareness of a life is not automatically that life’s subjectivity.
alternative_explanations: A defended subject-preserving relation could upgrade preservation-only to an enlarged-history proposal.
limitations: No argument that such a relation is impossible; its absence cannot be filled by naming the foundation.

claims.statement: No selected identity criterion automatically establishes universal subjecthood, timelessness, intention, goodness or moral authority; each needs an additional bridge and specified bearer.
limitations: Nine-component separation inherited from T01; not a denial of possible unification.

claims.statement: Reports of no succession, simultaneous content, indefinite duration and later narrative order require separate coding; testimony may support the occurrence of an experience without establishing the ontology attributed to it.
source_locators: Greyson p153; Timmermann Table1 and Limitations; project inference
alternative_explanations: An atemporal awareness could be narrated sequentially afterward; narrative order alone does not refute it.
limitations: No validated instrument here uniquely identifies H-T.

arguments.name: Psychological appropriation and a repaired continuity criterion
premises: A person is self-aware across relevant stages.
Past experience can be appropriately appropriated despite changing matter.
bridge_principles: Specify causal continuity without presupposing identity; add branching policy.
arguments.conclusion: Such continuity is a candidate basis for same-person persistence.
arguments.strongest_objection: Memories may duplicate, disappear or presuppose ownership.
arguments.strongest_reply: Project repair: overlapping causal links and a nonbranching clause avoid direct-memory transitivity failure; they still need independent justification.
unresolved_issues: Not all modern continuity accounts inspected; Parfit direct access failed.
Locke’s own theory is not identical to this repaired project model.

arguments.name: Thinking animal and biological persistence
premises: There is exactly one relevant thinker and that thinker is the person.
bridge_principles: Identity preserves the organism’s genuine persistence conditions, once specified.
arguments.conclusion: The human person is that organism; a disembodied copy alone does not preserve it.
arguments.strongest_objection: A transplanted cerebrum seems to carry the person; or the strict thinker is a soul/constituted subject.
arguments.strongest_reply: Olson presses costs of denying organism thought or multiplying thinkers; psychological evidence/concern may be mistaken for constitution.
unresolved_issues: Unique-thinker and strict animal-thinking premises contested.
Animalism alone is not a complete theory of death, resurrection or animal persistence.

arguments.name: Simple subject through qualitative change
premises: A hypothetical split leaves two equally psychologically supported candidates.
There is a determinate fact about which, if either, is the earlier subject beyond the total qualitative facts.
bridge_principles: Indeterminacy of accessible evidence reflects an additional bearer fact.
That fact requires an immaterial essential part.
arguments.conclusion: A soul is the candidate identity bearer.
arguments.strongest_objection: Epistemic underdetermination does not entail an immaterial entity; deny further-fact premise or specify a physical/causal identity rule.
arguments.strongest_reply: Charitable project reply: first-person numerical identity is not exhausted by descriptive similarity; the defender must argue that fact is real and immaterial, not merely unknowable.
unresolved_issues: Short essay does not resolve all technical objections.
A surviving soul and continuing experience require additional persistence/activation premises; simplicity is not immortality.

arguments.name: Enlarged first-person history beyond bodily life
premises: The foundation grounds a concrete first-person history, not merely an information record.
The history includes subjectivity outside the embodied-life boundary.
A defended relation unifies those portions as the same person.
bridge_principles: Ordered content can be grounded without successive changes in the foundation.
An explicit criterion—not resemblance alone—licenses same-subject attribution.
arguments.conclusion: M2 or enlargedM3 could satisfy H-S with foundation-level H-T.
arguments.strongest_objection: The asserted ownership/extension may restate survival; a universal knower can preserve a finite life without the person continuing.
arguments.strongest_reply: Treat subjectivity and individuation as substantive ontology with identifiable constraints; this blocks dismissal by definition but adds explanatory/evidential costs.
unresolved_issues: No observation here establishes enlarged history.
Strict organism criterion rejects disembodied extension unless same-organism relation defended.
Timeless individual model must explain non-successive awareness; the temporal-individual model does not solve that separate issue.

arguments.name: Temporal phenomenology under competing interpretations
premises: Altered-time reports are documented as reports.
Drug-context scale overlap is observed in one bounded design.
bridge_principles: Phenomenological resemblance alone does not identify mechanism or ontology.
arguments.conclusion: The reports motivate investigation but do not discriminate H-T/H-S without timing, identity and access evidence.
arguments.strongest_objection: Survival interpretation: coherent first-person reports and striking information may reveal real access beyond the body; instruments may miss their distinctiveness.
arguments.strongest_reply: Ordinary alternative has demonstrated drug-context overlap, while the survival reply correctly notes that inducing a resemblance need not explain a given case. Seek prospective, independently scored information and resolved timing; separately ask what identity relation it supports.
unresolved_issues: No same-mechanism conclusion; no inference of equal support.
No result here crosses irreversible bodily death under H-S.

cases.name: Timmermann2018 DMT and NDE-scale comparison
cases.underlying_event_or_sample: 13 healthy psychedelic-experienced volunteers measured after placebo and DMT; separate13-person retrospectively recruited NDE comparator.

chronology.detail: Fixed placebo-first, DMT one week later; single blind; report after effects subsided.
NDE questionnaire delay months–15years, mean7years; recruitment ComaScienceGroup/IANDSFrance/Flanders.

denominators.NDE_comparator_selection: above standard threshold; paper uses above/≥7 language; no raw boundary-score list

access_gaps: No participant-level data or separately reported EEG inspected.
Comparator overlap with C-T08-007 or other Liège/IANDS studies unestablished; do not add sample sizes.
Published comparator sex counts7female/6male differ from experimental6female/7male despite described age/gender matching; exact pair matching not supplied.
design_limits: Small purposive sample, prior psychedelic exposure, fixed order, single blindness, expectancy/priming, variable dose, retrospective comparator selection and reporting delay.
No objective performance time-perception task; EEG results outside inspectedarticle.
